newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks close mixed in lethargic trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks close mixed in lethargic trade.

text.p: ** (1015 GMT) - Bombay blue chips crawl higher in mixed
trade on last day of weekly account
** Bombay share index ends 16.32 points, or 0.40 percent,
percent up at a provisional 4,132.88 after surpassing
its old 52-week high of 4,148.99 at 4,153.80
** Reliance stock tumbles 3 percent on sharp bout of
institutional profit-taking after libearl -- one for one
bonus issue announced by firm on Thursday
** Gujarat Ambuja soars 19.25 rupees, or six percent, at
328.0 on market talk about a possible bonus share issue
** National exchange index up 2.20 points at 1,170.40
Stock prices crawled ahead at the Bombay exchange on Thursday amid lacklustre trade due to end-account considerations, traders said.
They said shares of bellwether Reliance Industries fell victim to a sharp bout of institutional profit-taking after the firm's liberal one for one bonus share announcement.
Reliance tumbled 12.25 rupees, or three percent, to end near the day's low at 365.0 with 7.34 million shares changing hands at the Bombay Stock Exchange.
At the National Stock Exchange, the stock fell 8.80 rupees to end at 370.0.
"What happened today was, that there was a lot of profit-booking in the stock," said Prashant Purker, head of institutional sales at Peregrine Capital India.
"End-account factors also obviously affected the price."

Reliance shares hit a new 52-week high of 388.0 on Thursday after the company announced a liberal one-for-one bonus share issue, suprising market participants. But heavy offloading by foreign institutions capped the price rise.
Traders said the stock could see sharp swings next week ahead of Tuesday's last day of trade account at the National Stock Exchange.
The Bombay share index ended this week 49.84 points, or over one percent higher, at an unoffical close of 4,132.88, thus gaining nearly 12 percent in the last five straight weeks.
Among other stocks, shares of Gujarat Ambuja Cement jumped six percent to close at 328.0 on market rumours about a possible bonus share issue being considered by the company.
Officials from Gujarat Ambuja Cement were not immediately available for comment.
Tata Power fell 4.50 rupees to 133.50 after the firm on Thursday said its net profit fell to 1.14 billion rupees for the year ending March 31, 1997 against 2.23 billion last year.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
